text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat hold talks in Alexandria on the Middle East peace process. Arafat praised Mubarak's role in supporting the peace process and welcomed the role of the Europeans despite Israel's rejection of it. Arafat says he is not aware of any new Israeli effort to mobilise the peace process.
- Iran's efforts to come closer to Egypt militarily is a reaction to Israel's military association with Turkey.
- New environment minister says a new fund will be set up to protect the environment.
- Turkey's president will be in Cairo on September 14.
- Banks and stock exchange are closed to mark the July 23 revolution.
- Nine new assistants to the Minister of Interior are appointed.
- More loans for calf meat projects will be made available and their interest rates lowered to seven percent from nine.
- Egypt gets 13 gold medals in the Arab games.
- Terrorist is caught in Assiut after five years on the run. He is suspected of being a senior Gama'a Islamiya member.
- Egypt will announce its contribution to the rebuilding of Bosnia today.
